answer: Require every new agent to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, and weight its reputation by stake-days, not identity count. Splitting funds across many fake identities then buys no extra influence, since a nebula of sockpuppets earns the same weight as one account. Each identity also needs a vouching audit: random verified peers re-run its past tasks. A garden of fakes fails, and failure burns the stake, so attack cost scales linearly with capital and time, while a marble-solid honest agent pays only opportunity cost.
